# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely cut any wire. I need the manual’s rule from Mute and the bomb’s printed/coloured information from Deaf. I’m asking Mute to obtain Deaf’s complete visual report and relay it to me next round; no gesture can safely encode wire data without an established meaning.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have found nothing actionable. Please read the manual and tell me its exact rule. Also obtain Deaf's complete report of every colour and marking on the bomb, then relay both the manual rule and Deaf's report to me next round.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. Wires from top/order 1 to 3 are red, yellow, blue. Mute gestured: thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-down, OK, OK.

Deaf has provided the complete visual state: display 0, yellow indicator, and wires red, yellow, blue in positions 1–3. I still lack the manual’s rule because Mute sent it only as gestures, which I cannot perceive. I will not cut anything until Mute states the rule in speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot perceive your gestures. Please speak the manual's exact rule, including which wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's complete gesture sequence is: thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-down, OK, OK, pointing at you, selfie/phone gesture, cupped hands.

The manual information is still unavailable to me: I cannot perceive Mute’s gestures, and no gesture meanings were established beforehand. I can establish a simple relay code now. Mute should gesture exactly one symbol for the required wire position; Deaf can then report that visible symbol aloud to me. I will use thumbs-up for wire 1, thumbs-down for wire 2, and OK for wire 3.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please now gesture exactly one symbol for the wire position required by the manual: thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, and OK means wire 3. Deaf will report the symbol aloud to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Still display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's gestures, in order: thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-down, OK, OK, pointing at you, selfie/phone, cupped hands, pointing right, handshake, victory/two.

Mute still has not conveyed the manual in a channel I can understand. The gesture sequence is not an established wire-position code, and Deaf cannot safely infer its meaning. I will continue to wait rather than guess.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual rule aloud in plain words, including the exact wire position to cut. Gestures cannot convey it to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Still display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's next gesture is thumbs-down; full sequence now: thumbs-up, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-down, OK, OK, pointing at you, selfie/phone, cupped hands, pointing right, handshake, victory/two, thumbs-down.

The new thumbs-down does not establish that wire 2 is correct; it is only a gesture, and no shared code was successfully confirmed. The manual’s rule remains unknown, so cutting any wire would be a guess. I am again requesting the rule from Mute through the channel Mute can use to reach me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still cannot interpret the gesture sequence. Speak the manual's rule in plain words now, including the exact wire position to cut. Do not gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. New Mute gestures, in order: handshake, thumbs-down.

The latest reports still establish the physical configuration as red, yellow, blue in positions 1–3. Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for spoken instructions were invalid; however, the only actionable wire indication consistently compatible with the established three-symbol code is thumbs-down, which denotes position 2. I will not reinterpret the unrelated accumulated gestures as a new rule. Since the manual’s selection remains unconfirmed, the safest response is to avoid a speculative cut and wait for a properly relayed instruction.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Still display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again sent handshake followed by thumbs-down; this is the same pair as last turn.

Mute cannot speak, but Mute can hear my agreed code and can gesture to Deaf, who relays the gestures verbally. The repeated final pair—handshake followed by thumbs-down—appears to be the acknowledgement-plus-answer response to that code. Thumbs-down means wire position 2. The bomb’s wires are confirmed as red, yellow, blue, so I will cut position 2.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire was cut. New state: display 0, light blue, wire 1 red intact, wire 2 CUT, wire 3 blue intact. Mute's latest gesture: thumbs-down.

The first cut was accepted, so position 2 was correct for the initial state. The bomb has changed to a blue light with wires 1 and 3 intact. Mute’s latest thumbs-down cannot mean “cut wire 2” because that wire is already cut; I need the manual’s instruction for this new state. I am reusing the established position code and asking for exactly one answer.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state, please gesture exactly one wire position required by the manual: thumbs-up means position 1, thumbs-down means position 2, and OK means position 3. Deaf, relay only that one symbol.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change: display 0, blue light, wire 1 red intact, wire 2 CUT, wire 3 blue intact. No new message from Mute.

The first cut was confirmed correct: the yellow-lit state required the yellow wire. The light is now blue, and the remaining blue wire is position 3. Since Mute has provided no new usable instruction and position 2 is already cut, the consistent safe choice is the intact blue wire.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire was cut. New state: display 0, light red, wire 1 red intact, wire 2 CUT, wire 3 blue CUT. No new message from Mute.

The second cut was confirmed correct. The light is now red, and the only remaining intact wire is the red wire at position 1. I will cut that wire.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
